title: LIBS 7102 · Lecture 5
subtitle: Act utilitarianism II: dark patterns and Canadian law, how not to describe utilitarianism, Mill's three objections, Nozick and the proof, aggregation, negative responsibility, promises, punishment, justice, and Singer on impartiality and supererogation
description: Lecture 5 of LIBS 7102: dark patterns, the FTC, the EU and Canada's PIPEDA, CASL and Bill C-27; consent and avuncular ethics; the essay revisions: not "for the majority", not cost-benefit, not "right because it causes happiness", the three-step procedure and why it is act utilitarianism; the doctrine of swine, too high for humanity and lack of time with Mill's replies and Sandel's doctors; psychological and normative hedonism, Nozick's experience machine and Mill's proof; aggregating utility, the strong doctrine of negative responsibility, trivial actions and the dying man's promise; rehabilitation, deterrence and vengeance, and Peter and Sarah's pay; Singer's Famine, Affluence and Morality, impartiality, the three kids and the threshold of supererogation; the fourteen objections. Practice answers U1, U2, U4 to U15 and a 22-item mock quiz.
intro:
:::exam Midterm facts
**Midterm: Wednesday Oct 28, in class.** Closed book, two hours, on paper, 20 % of the course. You write four or five two-paragraph answers, choosing from about six (for example, answer 4 of 6). Questions cover lectures 1 to 5 and are taken from the practice list (rare) or very similar to it (typical), often paired with a computing case or asking you to argue a side. With Lecture 4 it feeds fifteen of the twenty-five listed practice questions; this lecture alone owns fourteen of them.
:::

lessons.title: Dark patterns can be legal in Canada and still wrong, and act utilitarianism judges each one
Utilitarianism maximizes total utility, not happiness for the majority or benefits over costs
Mill answers three objections: the doctrine of swine, too high for humanity, lack of time
Nozick's experience machine and Mill's proof put hedonism in doubt
Adding utility lets small pleasures outweigh great harms, and promises bind only when they pay
Punishment and justice have only derivative value for a utilitarian
Singer: distance does not matter, and nothing is beyond the call of duty
Fourteen objections a utilitarian must be able to answer
